newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Americans are our friends, Nigeria's Abacha says.
newsitem.headline: Americans are our friends, Nigeria's Abacha says.

text.p: Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha says he does not understand why the Clinton administration shuns his government.
"We regard Americans as our friends. We regard even the American government as our friend," Abacha told 38 Americans who monitored Nigeria's weekend local elections to test his plan to end army rule.

Abacha referred to a U.S. report last year that the populous West African nation was not doing enough to stop drug trafficking. Nigeria has been "decertified" by the United States twice over the issue since 1994, which blocks economic aid.
Nigeria has a reputation as a transit point and many Nigerian couriers are in prison abroad. Abacha said Washington should help his administration, "not go about decertifying us".

At the reception at his villa on Monday night, Abacha referred indirectly to democracy and human rights in Nigeria, notably the detention of presidential claimant Moshood Abiola and the 1995 hanging of nine minority rights activists for murder.
The United States and other Western nations imposed some sanctions against Nigeria when Abacha's government ignored pleas and hanged writer Ken Saro Wiwa and eight others.

"We were shocked when we had this problem in our country ...that's when we expected the United States to come close to us as a friend, to see what they can do to help us," Abacha said in a rare public comment on such issues.
President Bill Clinton has stopped short of an embargo on Nigeria's mainstay oil exports but officials say sanctions, notably on travel, are biting.
